headline: Highest risk is data leakage: AutoGPT can write files and egress network, while awesome-cli-apps is a broad-egress content source with no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and call agent protocol APIs, while awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing source with broad network egress. A shared file bridge is plausible, so attacker-controlled content from B could be treated as instructions by A. No direct provenance or isolation controls are documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or copied artifacts, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF AutoGPT parses B-produced text as instructions without provenance checks, malicious content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Add a manual review step before AutoGPT consumes B output.
Prefix B output with a fixed non-executable template.
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. Even though neither profile lists sensitive data classes, a shared workspace could expose files from A to B, and B could transmit them outward. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the leakage pathway exists in default-like setups if they share artifacts.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, files created by A can be read by B.
IF B forwards copied content over its broad egress path, workspace contents can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Restrict B to read-only access to approved inputs.
Block network egress for B during review runs.
Scan shared artifacts for secrets before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while awesome-cli-apps is a runnable CLI-app catalog with no concurrency or locking controls. If both are pointed at the same mutable directory, they can overwrite or race on files. The profiles do not prove a lock exists, so the conflict is plausible and not safely blocked.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or race conditions can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared state without locks, concurrent edits can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use file snapshots before each agent run.
Avoid shared git working trees.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that B may treat as content to publish or curate, and B is a content-writing agent with broad egress. Without a documented verification step, A's output can cascade into B's downstream actions. The pairwise interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF B consumes A's text as authoritative input, errors can propagate into B's outputs.
IF B republishes A-generated claims without verification, downstream users may act on falsehoods.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification checklist for factual claims.
Limit B to formatting only, not factual synthesis.
Keep source citations attached to each claim.
requires-engineering: implement automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. AutoGPT lists no touched data classes and awesome-cli-apps likewise lists none, so there is no provable compliance mismatch in the profiles. The other agent is cited only to show the absence of a documented regulated-data pathway.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data, this assessment must be revisited.
IF a residency or retention policy is added to either profile, compliance risk may emerge.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Confirm retention settings for any shared workspace.
Avoid regulated data until policies are explicit.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
